ك.ف.ر.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses kafara only in modern senses (blaspheme, renege Islam, atone). In the Quran it means to disbelieve or deny, and also to be ungrateful (e.g. 2:152, 14:7). Added 2026-11-03.

#.ت.#.why: The lexicon reads the Form IV imperative آتِ (give!) only as the noun 'coming'; it glosses the verb آتَى as 'give; offer' elsewhere, so 'give' is attested for this root. Quranic use: 2:201, 17:26. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root with its weak radicals as #.ت.#.

#.ل.#.why: The lexicon glosses tawallā only as 'take charge of; be in charge of'. In the Quran its most frequent sense is to turn away (تَوَلَّى عَنْ), e.g. 37:90, 37:174, 80:1. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (و.ل.ي) with its weak radicals as #.ل.#.

#.ح.#.why: The lexicon glosses awḥā as 'inspire; suggest' only. In the Quran it is the verb of divine revelation (وَحْي), e.g. 42:3, 53:4. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (و.ح.ي) as #.ح.#.

ل.ق.#.why: The lexicon reads the Form IV imperative أَلْقِ (throw!) only as 'shine' (root أ.ل.ق) or 'meet'; it glosses the verb أَلْقَى as 'deliver; throw' elsewhere, so 'throw' is attested for this root. Quranic use: 20:19, 20:69. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ل.ق.ي) as ل.ق.#.

ح.ب.ب.why: The lexicon reads the Form IV imperative أَحْبِبْ (love!) only as the first person 'I endear'; it glosses the verb أَحَبَّ as 'love; like' elsewhere, so 'love' is attested for this root. Added 2026-11-03.

ر.ز.ق.why: The lexicon glosses razaqa only as 'bestow; endow' (and the passive 'be bestowed'). In the Quran it is the verb of God providing sustenance, e.g. 2:3, 42:19, 51:58; 'provide' is the standard rendering. Added 2026-11-03.

ع.ق.ل.why: The lexicon glosses ʿaqala as a verb only as 'make reasonable' / 'be reasonable; be sensible'. In the Quran it means to understand or use one's reason (2:75 مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ, the refrain أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ 2:44). Added 2026-11-03.

ح.#.#.why: The lexicon reads the Form IV past أَحْيَا only as the first-person 'I live; experience' (أَحْيَا of Form I); it glosses other forms of the verb as 'enliven', so the causative sense is attested for this root. Quranic use: 2:28, 53:44 (أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا). Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ح.ي.ي) as ح.#.#.

ح.س.ب.why: The lexicon glosses ḥasiba only as 'compute; charge' / 'regard; consider', and reads the past حَسِبَ only as the preposition 'according to'. In the Quran it means to think or suppose (23:115 أَفَحَسِبْتُمْ, 104:3 يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ). Added 2026-11-03.

ر.#.#.why: The lexicon has no Form IV arā 'to show': it reads أَرَى, يُرِي and أُرِي only as Form I 'see; think' or 'kindle'. In the Quran the causative sense is frequent (20:56 أَرَيْنَاهُ آيَاتِنَا, 20:23 لِنُرِيَكَ). Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ر.أ.ي) as ر.#.#.

ب.ش.ر.why: The lexicon glosses bashshara only as 'rejoice; augur; evangelize' (and 'peel'). In the Quran it means to give good news, to announce glad tidings, e.g. 15:53, 37:101, 84:24. Added 2026-11-03.

ح.ش.ر.why: The lexicon reads the verb حَشَرَ only as the noun 'congregation; assemblage'; it has no verbal gloss. In the Quran ḥashara means to gather, to assemble, e.g. 19:85, 37:22. Added 2026-11-03.

ص.د.د.why: The lexicon glosses ṣadda only as 'repel; deter; resist'. In the Quran صَدَّ عَنْ is intransitive 'turn away' (4:61) and transitive 'hinder (others)' (47:1). Added 2026-11-03.

س.#.#.why: The lexicon glosses istawā only as 'be equivalent; be ripe'. In the Quran and in MSA it also means to rise, to settle (on), to be level, e.g. 11:44, 48:29, 53:6. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (س.و.ي) with its weak radicals as س.#.#.

ن.س.#.why: The lexicon reads the past نَسِيَ only as the noun nasy ('forgetfulness; oblivion'), although it glosses the other forms of this verb as 'forget' (نَسُوا, نَسِيتُ). Quranic use: 20:88, 20:115. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ن.س.ي) as ن.س.#.

ب.غ.#.why: The lexicon glosses ibtaghā only as 'desire; want'. Its Quranic and standard sense is to seek, e.g. 17:57, 23:7. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ب.غ.ي) as ب.غ.#.

ق.#.م.why: The lexicon glosses qāma only as 'undertake; carry out' and 'straighten'; it lacks the core sense to stand (up), to rise, e.g. 72:19, 73:2. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ق.و.م) as ق.#.م.

ع.ر.ض.why: The lexicon glosses Form IV aʿraḍa only as 'avoid; expose; exhibit'. In the Quran أَعْرَضَ عَنْ means to turn away (from), e.g. 32:30, 41:4. Added 2026-11-03.

ع.س.#.why: The analyzer reads عَسَى only as nouns ('night patrol', 'capable'); it has no reading of the inflexible verb, whose meaning is 'perhaps, it may be that', e.g. 2:216, 27:72. Added 2026-11-03. CAMeL writes this root (ع.س.ي) as ع.س.#.

ج.ه.د.why: The CAMeL lexicon glosses the verb jāhada only as 'wage war or Jihad (against)'; its own noun gloss for the root is 'striving; endeavoring'. In the Quran the verb is to strive and exert oneself (29:6, 29:69), which is the sense the practice sentences teach. Added 2026-11-04.

ع.ص.#.why: The lexicon glosses ʿaṣā only as 'resist; refuse'. In the Quran it means to disobey (20:93, 20:121, 18:69). Added 2026-11-04.

#.ذ.ن.why: The lexicon glosses adhina as 'authorize; listen' and 'announce'; its noun gloss for the root is 'permission; authorization'. In the Quran adhina li means to permit (9:43, 22:39). Added 2026-11-04.

ج.#.ب.why: The lexicon glosses istajāba only as 'comply; reply', while it glosses ajāba of the same root as 'answer'. In the Quran istajāba is to answer or respond (2:186, 8:24). Added 2026-11-04.

ف.ت.ن.why: The lexicon glosses fatana only as 'entice; torment' and 'be infatuated', yet glosses maftūn 'fascinated; charmed' and fātin 'tempting; charming' of the same root. The practice sentences use the everyday MSA sense 'to charm, captivate'. Added 2026-11-04.

غ.ن.#.why: The lexicon glosses aghnā as 'enrich; satisfy', but reads its imperative أَغْنِ only as other words (buzz, melodious, become rich). 'Enrich' is the root's own attested verb gloss. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:تُبْ.why: CAMeL reads the hollow imperative تُبْ (repent!, root ت.و.ب, cf. توبوا 66:8) only as تَبَّ 'perish' (root ت.ب.ب). A root exception would have to be filed under ت.ب.ب, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:ذَرِ.why: CAMeL reads the imperative ذَرْ / ذَرِ (leave! let!, root و.ذ.ر, cf. ذَرْهُمْ 15:3) only as a noun of ذ.ر.ر 'strewing'; it has no analysis under و.ذ.ر, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

س.ل.م.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses أَسْلَمَ only as 'hand over; surrender'. Its everyday sense — and the one learners meet first — is to become Muslim, to embrace Islam (cf. أَسْلَمَ in 3:20, 49:17). Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:ارْجُوا.why: CAMeL reads the imperative ارْجُوا (hope!, root ر.ج.و, cf. وَارْجُوا 29:36) only as a form of أَرِجَ 'be aromatic' (root أ.ر.ج); it has no analysis under ر.ج.و, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

spelling:هَبْ.why: CAMeL reads the imperative هَبْ (grant!, root و.ه.ب, cf. هَبْ لِي 3:38) only as هَبَّ 'blow, get up' (root ه.ب.ب); it has no analysis under و.ه.ب, so it is excepted by this spelling alone. Added 2026-11-04.

ح.ق.ق.why: The CAMeL MSA lexicon glosses the verb حَقَّ only as 'be correct; be right'. Its other core sense — to become due, binding or incumbent (حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ, cf. فَحَقَّ عَلَيْنَا قَوْلُ رَبِّنَا 37:31, حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ 10:33) — is missing. Added 2026-11-04.
